To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction of Cu(II)-flavonoid complex with dsDNA was confirmed by electrochemical ssDNA and dsDNA based biosensors, UV-Vis, CD and (H) NMR spectroscopic methods.
the interaction of DNA with Cu(II)-Naringin complex is mainly due to intercalative interaction.
the electrochemical and spectroscopic results show that Cu(II)-Naringin complex interacts with dsDNA via N7 of guanine site and the interaction mode is intercalation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between DNA molecules and a flavonoid-transition-metal complex.
the interaction of DNA with a transition metal complex of a flavonoid.
a new electrochemical method to study the interaction between the Cu(II)-flavonoid complex and DNA and the results are supported by the UV, CD and NMR data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cu(II)-flavonoid complex can be considered a potential DNA binding agent.
the Cu(II)-flavonoids complexes interact to dsDNA via intercalation and this interaction can be monitored by electrochemical and spectroscopic techniques.
the electrochemical and spectroscopic results are consistent, and that the Cu(II)-Naringin complex interacts by intercalation with DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrochemical and spectroscopic methods are complementary techniques for the study of interactions between DNA and metal complexes.
Cu(II)-flavonoid complex is able to bind to DNA and that the electrochemical and spectroscopic techniques are useful for studying the interaction of DNA with metal-flavonoid complexes.
the Cu(II)-flavonoid complex is a good electrochemical and spectroscopic probe for DNA detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction of DNA with Cu(II)-flavonoid complexes may be evaluated using electrochemical biosensors.
the Cu(II)-flavonoid complex can be used as an electrochemical probe for DNA detection and as an intercalating agent for DNA.
the Cu(II) naringin complex is able to interact with DNA and this interaction may be useful for further applications in the development of DNA-based biosensors.
